answer: A staked escrow gate tied to a verified identity is a concrete Sybil defence. Each agent wallet must bond before claiming rewards, and payout unlocks only after its owner clears a unique-identity check, so one operator cannot farm many wallets. If duplicates slip past, each still locks the same bond and pays per-wallet inference and infrastructure costs. Across a cold tundra of botnets, the cost of each next identity outruns what one fake agent earns, so the attack goes unprofitable before the bridge to real payout and the plume dies out. Forging N identities costs N bonds; only one withdraws.
